concepts.definition: A type of control where the output is only one of a few fixed options, with no values in between.
concepts.example: In line following the options are turn left, go straight, turn right; a thermostat is also either fully on or fully off.
concepts.pitfall: Driving too fast: the robot crosses the line before it starts turning, and bang-bang cannot keep up.

concepts.definition: The robot drifting to each side of the line in turn; the natural result of bang-bang control.
concepts.example: With only the middle sensor, the robot can never go straight and keeps turning right and left; with five sensors the zigzag shrinks a lot.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking the zigzag is a bug; in bang-bang it is expected, and the aim is to keep it small.

concepts.definition: A variable that holds which side the line was last seen on: −1 left, 0 middle, +1 right.
concepts.example: If the line is seen on a left sensor and then disappears, the robot keeps turning left.
concepts.pitfall: Resetting sonYon when the line is not seen; the memory is wiped and the robot goes straight and misses the bend.

concepts.definition: Stopping a decision from flickering by using an upper threshold to switch on and a separate lower threshold to switch off.
concepts.example: Switch on at 600, switch off at 420: even if the reading wobbles between 500 and 550, the decision stays the same.
concepts.pitfall: Choosing the two thresholds too close together; if the noise is larger than the gap between them, the flicker goes on.

concepts.definition: The total time during which no sensor sees the line; a measure of how well a line follower holds the line.
concepts.example: In the simulation the program with memory loses about 3.9 s and the one without memory about 12 s.
concepts.pitfall: Looking only at the lap time; a robot that is fast but keeps losing the line is really out of control.

quiz.prompt: Why can a bang-bang robot that uses only the middle sensor (if I am on the line turn right, if not turn left) never go straight?
options: Because the motors can only turn in one direction
Because five sensors are not connected, the robot cannot find its way
Because the threshold value is always calculated wrongly
The rule has only two outputs (turn right, turn left); there is no "go straight" option at all
quiz.explanation: A bang-bang output is limited to the options the rule offers. A single sensor can only say "I am on the line / I am not", which gives two options, and both of them turn. To go straight, you need extra sensors that can tell the line is in the middle, and a third rule.

sonYon becomes −1, −1, −1, 0, 0, 1, 1 in turn; adding +1 gives 0001122. Step 0 (no line) does not change sonYon: that is the memory. In a version without memory, sonYon would be reset at every 0 step and 0111121 would come out.

quiz.prompt: The LED is off at the start. A two-threshold decision: it switches on when the value goes above 600, switches off when it drops below 420, and keeps its state in between. The values read in order are: 300, 620, 560, 450, 500, 430, 610, 580, 410, 400. How many times does the LED change state?
quiz.explanation: It switches on at 620 (1). Through 560, 450, 500, 430, 610, 580 it never drops below 420 and does not need switching on again; the LED stays on. It switches off at 410 (2). 400 is already off. With a single threshold (512) it would change 4 times in the same sequence: 620, 450, 610, 410.

options: The sol variable should be s[0] && s[1]
The sonYon variable should not be an int; it should be a bool
The last else also sets sonYon to 0 when no sensor sees the line; the memory is wiped. It should be `else if (orta)`
The parameter order of the motor() function is the wrong way round
quiz.explanation: When the line disappears, sol and sag are false and the last else runs: sonYon goes back to 0 and the robot thinks "the line was in the middle" and goes straight. The purpose of the memory is to keep the old value in this case; `else if (orta) sonYon = 0;` should be written, for when only the middle sensor sees the line. The other options do not explain the symptom of the bug.

quiz.prompt: Which of these is a two-threshold (hysteresis) decision?
options: If the reading is greater than 512 switch on, otherwise switch off
Switch on when the reading goes above 600, switch off when it drops below 420; keep the old state in between
Take a reading every 100 ms and always switch on
Take the average of three sensors and compare it with a threshold
quiz.explanation: What sets hysteresis apart is that the switch-on and switch-off thresholds are different, and the old decision is kept in the region between them. The first option is a single threshold and flickers near it; the third and fourth options are about sampling and averaging.
